correctness.rationale:
Forward transport is valid because an \(f\)-ergodic measure has finitely many \(f^q\)-ergodic components cyclically permuted by \(f\); they have equal \(f^q\)-entropy, hence each has \(q\) times the original entropy. Conversely, for an \(f^q\)-witness \((K,
u)\), the finite union \(\Lambda= igcup_{j=0}^{q-1}f^jK\) is compact and \(f\)-invariant, each phase is conjugate for \(f^q\), and finite-union entropy gives the correct topological value. The average \(q^{-1}\sum_j f_*^j
u\) is \(f\)-invariant and is \(f\)-ergodic because every \(f\)-invariant measurable set is also \(f^q\)-invariant for \(
u\). Entropy affinity and the power law then give the target metric entropy. Invertibility is used in the phase conjugacies.

value.rationale: Positive iteration is the canonical finite resampling operation in discrete dynamics. Showing exact invariance of a newly introduced coupled topological/metric realization property, while resolving the genuine losses of ergodicity and subsystem invariance under powers, is a useful structural closure theorem rather than a parameter substitution.
residual_risks: A short folklore observation or lecture note could contain the same power-invariance lemma without searchable indexing.

final_claim: For every homeomorphism \(f\) of a compact metric space and every integer \(q\ge1\), entropy flexibility is invariant under passing to \(f^q\); witnesses transport forward by taking an \(f^q\)-ergodic component and backward by finite phase union and phase averaging, with entropy scaled by \(q\).
limitations: The converse is proved for homeomorphisms; no non-invertible analogue is asserted.
Strict ergodicity of a particular witness need not survive every power.
